Every repro re-run from the current tree, with a pure-HEAD mirror (git archive HEAD) and a current-tree-with-HEAD-eval/api.py hybrid built outside the repo to get the BEFORE half honestly.

WHAT I CONFIRMED BY RUNNING IT. The suite is exactly what they report: ownership '12 checks + 18 self-test cases, 0 failing'; contract '14 checks + 46 self-test cases, 1 failing' with the single line 'FAIL K12'; census 7/0; assemble 9/0; couplings 4/0; derive '575 oracle cases, 0 mismatches'. The pure-HEAD mirror runs 0 failing on all five, and a hybrid tree that is the current tree with ONLY src/eval/api.py reverted to HEAD makes K12 PASS again -- so the one red check is caused by their edit and by nothing else, which is what they say. Their proposed one-clause repair to spine/compose.py::DEFERRED_ENTRY_POINTS['EVAL.verification_fit'] applies cleanly (1 occurrence of the FIND text) and, in a faithful scratch copy of the current tree, takes tests/test_contract.py to '14 checks + 46 self-test cases, 0 failing'. Verified, not taken on trust.

23 couplings, 19 wires of 25, 4 intra-package, at HEAD AND today -- no wire was spent. NOT_WIRES holds 7 rows at both. EVAL is the destination of no Coupling and declares no d_ field. MEM's Store.__slots__ carries no verify field and MEM.open_store's own LEVERS READ line says in as many words that it does not read mem.verify, so the 'recover it from store_copy' option really is closed. `step` IS in K12's 126-value produced set, off RUN.new_clock's produces column ('step': RunClock.step (units.Windows)) -- I recomputed the set with the check's own helpers rather than reading the claim.

THE ONE I NARROWED. The capacity refusal is declared correctly and identically in the only two places that state the closed set. But its stated CONTROL -- 'cap.valve unchanged on all eight corners' -- is VACUOUS: on all eight of those corners cap.valve is UNREACHABLE by construction (both caps sit at the sentinel-resolved hard ceiling, 'no room to earn'), so that control could not have detected any interaction. On the corners where cap.valve IS reachable the change reintroduces the exact defect the same file repaired the same day: at CAP_TARGETS=both CAP_FAB_START=0 CAP_VOCAB_START=1000 LM_MASK_DEAD_ROWS=0 the expert arm is dead on arrival and every vocabulary lift is now refused by `dead_rows_unmasked`, and cap.valve still prints FIRED, 'an armed arm has room to earn'. Reproduced, both corners, in a fresh process each.

WHAT THEY DID NOT REPORT, ordered by how much it costs a reader. (1) A FALSE CITATION IN THREE PLACES, ALL THREE IN FILES THEY OWN: src/eval/api.py::<module>, src/eval/api.py::curve_probe and docs/04_CONTRACT.md::Q-EVAL-11 all say d_curve_bpb and d_shift_at are refused in spine/assemble.py::NOT_WIRES. They are not. NOT_WIRES holds exactly 7 candidates and neither is among them; both live in docs/04_CONTRACT.md section 0's separate 12-row 'Candidates examined and refused as wires' table -- a table whose OWN rows mark which entries are additionally in NOT_WIRES ('already refused in assemble.NOT_WIRES', 'd_seed is refused by name in NOT_WIRES'), so the document supplies the distinction the new paragraphs erase. The ARGUMENT is unaffected; the citation is wrong, in a tree whose O12 checks citation FORM and cannot check citation TRUTH. (2) The cap.valve interaction above. (3) src/capacity/api.py::<module>'s RECORD TYPES line for Valve.COUNTERS still says new_valve seeds 'the two caps, the two HARD ceilings and the two origins' while new_valve now seeds EIGHT keys -- it never named cap.targets and it does not name the cap.mask_dead_rows this edit added, though the neighbouring new_valve DID IT FIRE (2) line WAS updated for it. That paragraph exists because the Valve line 'omitted two of its own declared fields' once already. (4) The 'two edges left' miscount their own module docstring corrects SURVIVES UNCORRECTED in two more files -- src/eval/levers.py::<module> ('WIRE_BUDGET leaves room for two more edges in the whole tree') and src/capacity/levers.py::CAPLevers ('has room for two more edges in total') -- and docs/04_CONTRACT.md's correction paragraph names eval/api.py as the only carrier. Neither levers file is theirs, so this is residue, not a miss they could have fixed; but it is not reported anywhere.

THEIR OWN UNFINISHED ITEMS ARE ALL REAL. I re-verified the K12 residue (applies, turns contract green), both present-tense 'BYTE-IDENTICAL' sentences in spine/compose.py (still there, still present-tense, now false), and the assemble.py CAP.d_mask_dead_rows row's incompleteness. findings.detail: THE REFUSAL IS REAL AND CONSISTENT; THE CONTROL THEY OFFER FOR 'D15 IS UNDISTURBED' IS VACUOUS, AND OUTSIDE IT THE CHANGE REINTRODUCES D15's DEFECT ON THE VOCABULARY ARM. What holds: `dead_rows_unmasked` is in the closed set in observe's DID IT FIRE and in docs/04_CONTRACT.md's CAP section, and those are the ONLY two places in the tree that state the set (`grep -rn 'not_stalled|targets_off'` over src and docs returns src/capacity/api.py:491-492 and docs/04_CONTRACT.md:514-515 and nothing else); they are word-for-word compatible; `mask_dead` is bound at the top of new_valve so counters['cap.mask_dead_rows'] cannot NameError; the quoted assemble.py CAP.d_mask_dead_rows 'Reducible' sentence is verbatim; LM.mask_dead_rows really does default to False. The eight-corner control reproduces EXACTLY as stated -- I ran all eight in fresh processes and got cap.vocab_arm_honest reachable on vocab x {0,1} and both x {0,1} only, FIRED on vocab/1 and both/1 -- AND I ran the same eight against a HEAD copy of src and got byte-identical gate states, which is the honest way to show the gate is undisturbed. WHAT DOES NOT HOLD: 'cap.valve unchanged on all eight' is true and proves nothing, because cap.valve is UNREACHABLE on all eight (both starts are the sentinel, which resolves to the hard ceiling -- the file's own 'no room to earn'), so no interaction could show there. Set a soft cap with headroom and the interaction appears: cap.valve's `vocab_room = vocab_armed and 0 < cv < hard_vocab` never consults mask_dead, so on a run whose only liftable arm is the vocabulary arm with the mask off -- every lift now refused per flush -- cap.valve prints FIRED with the reason 'an armed arm has room to earn and a cap the population can reach'. That is 'FIRED, printed for a mechanism that cannot move', which is the sentence the SAME comment block uses to describe the defect it repaired on 2026-09-04, one condition later. The comment enumerates 'THREE WAYS AN ARMED ARM IS DEAD ON ARRIVAL'; this edit created a fourth and did not add it. SECOND, SMALLER NARROWING: the argument against option (B) is that a startup refusal 'would make CAP_TARGETS=vocab unrunnable on the shipped defaults (a capability removal)'. As implemented, the vocabulary arm cannot lift on those same defaults either -- the capability is removed in both designs; what moves is whether the operator is told at startup or has to read a histogram. The per-flush form is still the better of the two (the run proceeds, the other arm works, the count is visible) but the stated ground is weaker than presented. THIRD: nothing executable refuses anything today -- CAP.observe raises NotImplementedError -- so this is a contract-level fix, which is legitimate here, EXCEPT that new_valve's Gate reason is RUNTIME OUTPUT rendered on every compose(), and it now tells an operator 'THE LIFT IS REFUSED, NOT MERELY REPORTED' about a body that does not exist. The line it replaced erred the other way.
